sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Accidental damage, fire, theft and malicious damage to your vehicle, plus your liability to third parties under the Road Traffic Act.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Wear and tear, mechanical breakdown, unlicensed drivers and any loss caused by driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

sections.label: Costs and excess
sections.body: You pay the compulsory and any voluntary excess on each claim; the premium depends on your rating factors at quote or renewal.

sections.label: How to claim
sections.body: Report the incident through My Insura or our motor claims line; we appoint an approved repairer and agree the repair estimate.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Accidental damage to your own car where you are at fault, and damage from vandalism that is not linked to an attempted theft.

sections.label: Costs and excess
sections.body: Premiums are usually lower than comprehensive; excesses apply to fire and theft claims and are shown on your policy schedule.

sections.label: How to claim

sections.label: What's not covered

sections.label: Costs and excess
sections.body: The lowest-priced level of cover, though some drivers find comprehensive is similar in price after rating factors are applied.

sections.label: How to claim
sections.body: Tell us promptly about any incident involving another party and do not admit liability or agree a settlement without us.

sections.label: What is an excess
sections.body: The amount you contribute to a claim; it is made up of a compulsory excess set by us and any voluntary excess you choose.

sections.label: Choosing a voluntary excess
sections.body: A higher voluntary excess usually lowers your premium but means paying more if you claim, so pick an amount you could afford.

sections.label: Young and inexperienced driver excess
sections.body: An additional compulsory excess may apply where the driver is under 25 or has held a licence for less than a year.

sections.label: When the excess is not charged

sections.body: Insurers rate drivers under 25 and those new to driving as higher risk, which increases premiums and excesses.

sections.label: Ways to reduce the cost
sections.body: Choosing a smaller engine, a higher voluntary excess, a telematics policy or being named on a parent's policy can help.

sections.label: Telling us about a change
sections.body: Tell us as soon as your use changes; failing to do so could lead to a claim being reduced or declined.

sections.label: If you break down or crash abroad

sections.label: Earning your discount
sections.body: You earn one year for each full year you hold a policy without a claim where we pay out and cannot recover our costs.

sections.label: What happens when you claim
sections.body: A claim you are at fault for normally reduces your discount by two years, or sets it back to a lower step.

sections.label: Using a company car or other vehicle
sections.body: Time driving another car as a named driver or on a company vehicle may sometimes count, if you hold written proof.

sections.label: Discount if you stop driving
sections.body: Your discount is usually valid for two years after a policy ends, so you can restart cover without losing it.

sections.label: Proof after you cancel

sections.label: Information on the letter
sections.body: It shows the policyholder, the number of years, the dates of cover and whether the discount is protected.

sections.label: If your proof is lost or wrong
sections.body: Ask us for a replacement through secure messages; we will reissue the document at no charge.

sections.label: Cost of protection
sections.body: Pricing depends on how many years of discount you hold; it is shown separately at quote and renewal.

sections.label: When it does not apply
sections.body: Protection may not apply to a claim after a conviction for a serious driving offence or a lapse in cover.

sections.label: Adding or removing protection
sections.body: Change this on My Insura; you will be asked to confirm that you have no claims you have not told us about.

sections.label: How telematics works
sections.body: A small device or our app records speed, braking, cornering, time of day and mileage, and scores each journey.

sections.label: Your driving score
sections.body: Scores are reviewed monthly; a consistently good score earns a premium reduction at renewal.

sections.label: Mileage and night driving
sections.body: Policies set a mileage limit, and regular driving between midnight and 5am may reduce your score.

sections.label: Fitting, returning and privacy
sections.body: A fitter installs the box free; return it within 30 days if you cancel; data is kept as described in our privacy notice.

sections.label: Rebuild cost and sum insured
sections.body: Your sum insured should equal the cost of rebuilding the property, not its market value.

sections.label: Mortgage lender requirements

sections.label: Calculating your sum insured
sections.body: Add up replacement-as-new values room by room; underinsuring may reduce any claim payment.

sections.label: Home contents away from home

sections.label: Excess on a combined claim

sections.label: Switching to combined cover
